fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Vehicle Parking Area; Storage Area; Equipment Storage Area; Access Drive; Open Green Space; Street Frontage
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Multiple Structures; Limited Turnaround Space; Dense Vegetation
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker visible from the street at the driveway entrance.
• Mark the access drive entrance with reflective posts on both sides so it is visible at night or in low visibility conditions.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles and equipment so emergency vehicles can reach both structures without obstruction.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain clearance wide enough for an emergency vehicle on each side.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain overhead clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Identify and mark a turnaround point near the main residence so responding crews do not have to back a long distance to the street.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between buildings on foot.
• Post the address number on both the main residence and the detached structure so responders can quickly identify each building.
• Keep the storage and equipment areas clear of the access drive so they do not narrow or block the path for emergency vehicles.
• If the access drive has a gate, keep it unlocked or install a lock box accessible to emergency responders.

wildfire.conditions: Large Wood Pile; Large Wood Pile; Large Wood Pile; Large Wood Pile; Large Wood Pile; Scattered Trees; Scattered Trees; Open Terrain; Tall Grass Area; Single Access Route; Adequate Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Move the wood piles away from the house and any outbuildings, keeping at least 30 feet of separation between the piles and structures.
• Separate the wood piles from each other so they are not stacked or grouped in a continuous row.
• Store wood piles on bare ground or gravel, not on dry grass or dead vegetation.
• Clear tall grass directly around and beneath each wood pile.
• Cut and remove tall grass in open areas near the house and other structures.
• Keep tall grass mowed short in areas between the wood piles and the house.
• Trim low branches from scattered trees to reduce the chance of fire climbing from grass into the tree canopy.
• Remove dead branches and dry material from beneath scattered trees.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and brush so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate under smoky or low-visibility conditions.
